thread:
Incident Bot: [PAGER] high_latency: /v1/chat completions p99 = 820ms (>500ms) for 5m. alert_id=ALERT-998
Alyssa: grabbing the traces, oncall here. sending headsup to infra.
Alyssa: can someone check routing from edge -> region-us-central? I see a small spike in queue depth.
Matt: eyeballing infra metrics now. node pool scaling seems fine. CPU low, but one host in pool shows GPU memory thrash.
Sana: copying logs to gist, link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/temp-logs-824 (logs from 10:41-10:50)
Alyssa: thx. initial impact: ~4% requests for /v1/chat experienced >500ms p99, mostly for model=mistral-v0-large and route=chat-stream.
Joel: any customer-facing incidents yet? Pager said no customer-wide escalations.
Alyssa: no escalations, but a few error rates rose transiently. caught in alerts. looks like KV cache misses spiked.
Matt: I see KV cache churn on the GPU host. maybe model shards rebalanced. rolling redeploy to the pool happened 20m ago.
Sana: quick mitigation: pin requests for heavy models to dedicated pool version 'dedicated-a' until we finish root cause.
Alyssa: agreed. Matt can you add a routing override? small script works: 
```
# temp route override
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: route-overrides
data:
  /v1/chat: "dedicated-a"
EOF
```
Matt: applied override, traffic steering in progress. I'll monitor p99.
Incident Bot: Route override set by Matt at 1972458720
Alyssa: p99 dropped to 460ms on the affected model group after override. Good.
Sana: for post-incident, we should: 1) adjust p95/p99 alert rules to be per-model-group, 2) add a dashboard showing cache hit rate vs latency, 3) update runbook with routing override steps.
Matt: Agreed. Current alert rule is too coarse, fires when small noisy models increase latency. Proposal: keep global p95 at 350ms, but per-model p99 thresholds: mistral-v0-large = 700ms, redwood-llama2-13b = 600ms, small models = 450ms. Also add a 5m suppression for routable rollouts.
Alyssa: vote? :thumbsup: for the per-model p99s. We need a temporary window for the change then reevaluate after 24h of telemetry.
Joel: I'll take the handoff in 30m. Can we codify the change as a config PR so it can be rolled back? 
Sana: creating PR now: github.com/redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/1428 - contains per-model rules and a new dashboard definition. brief snippet in PR description:
```
- alert: Chat_Completions_P99_Per_Model
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(latency_bucket{route="/v1/chat", model=~"mistral.*|llama2.*|redwood.*"}[5m])) by (le, model)) > (model_threshold)
  for: 5m
```
Alyssa: nice. Matt will coordinate canary change: apply to non-production first, then 10% production, then 100% if stable.
Matt: rolling canary: step1 non-prod apply now, step2 10% prod in 15m, monitor p99, then 100% if stable 30m later. I'll post statuses.
Incident Bot: Canary step applied to non-prod at 1972459100
Matt: non-prod looks good. 10% prod roll in 5m.
Alyssa: reminder: document customer impact thread in incidents channel if any customer notes pop up. We should tag customers with requests that hit p99.
Joel: taking over oncall in 30m. I'll watch the dashboard and cancel overrides once cluster stabilizes and cache warms.
Sana: follow-ups for postmortem: - add cache hit ratio graph to service dashboard, - consider KV cache TTL tuning, - inspect redeploy timing to avoid shard churn during peak.
Alyssa: adding action items to runbook and assigning owners in the PR. I'll draft a short incident summary for the postmortem.
Joel: thanks. handing off now. if anything pages, ping me @joel and I'll escalate.
Alyssa: thanks team. closing pager for now; reopen if p99 > threshold again.
Incident Bot: Pager resolved at 1972460400 (manual close by Alyssa)
